news_drafts.headline: Bridgend forecasts £628,000 overspend for 2026-27, with £3.155m directorate overspends offset by council-wide underspends
news_drafts.lead:
Bridgend council's Cabinet was told that the council expects to end 2026-27 with a net overspend of £628,000, based on the position at 30 September 2026. The figure combines a £3.155m net overspend across council directorates with a £2.527m net underspend on council-wide budgets. Of that underspend, £2.432m is additional projected interest on the council's investments.

Adult Social Care accounts for much of the directorate overspend. It was forecast at the second quarter to overspend by £3.395m for the year, up £1.667m from the £1.728m forecast at the first quarter. The report points to older people's homecare, where care hours rose from 9,850 to 10,235 between the two quarters. The council attributes this to demographic pressure and to rapid hospital discharge, with business continuity incidents at the Health Board affecting reablement (short-term support to help people regain independence at home). It is reviewing reablement and "right-sizing" care packages within six weeks.

The 2026-27 savings programme (the cuts and efficiencies committed to balance the budget) is forecast to deliver £2.058m against a £2.348m target, a £290,000 shortfall. A prior-year proposal to cut supported living by £190,000 "is no longer deliverable", and a £295,000 cultural services saving is being covered from money set aside. School budgets are forecast to be £6.537m in deficit, against £6.529m at the first quarter. Forty-six schools, 78% of the total, project deficits of £7.672m, while 13 project surpluses of £1.135m.

news_drafts.headline: Bridgend's 2025-26 accounts receive unqualified audit opinion
news_drafts.lead: The Auditor General for Wales intends to issue an unqualified audit opinion on Bridgend's 2025-26 accounts, confirming they give a true and fair view and were properly prepared. However, auditors identified several control weaknesses. The initial draft accounts did not include transactions and balances from the South East Wales Corporate Joint Committee, a shared body run with other councils, which were added only in a revised draft submitted in September. Auditors found that a category of asset valuations had not been properly indexed, a control gap that could become cumulatively significant over the five-year valuation cycle, though the current-year impact is not significant. Additionally, the minimum revenue provision—the amount set aside annually from the budget to repay borrowing—was understated by £0.291 million due to the accounting treatment of the Rhiw property purchase. All issues were corrected during the audit.

news_drafts.headline: Bridgend's 2025-26 accounts certified early, but audit found multiple errors in draft figures
news_drafts.lead: Bridgend Council's external auditors are certifying the 2025-26 accounts on 25 September, six days ahead of the statutory 30 September deadline. The Governance and Audit Committee was told that auditors had identified a series of misstatements in the draft accounts, all later corrected by council officers. These included member allowances overstated by £0.061 million, minimum revenue provision (the amount the council must set aside from each year's budget to repay past borrowing) understated by £0.291 million, transactions from the South East Wales Corporate Joint Committee initially omitted, and property valuations that had not been updated. The auditor also flagged that indexation, the annual revaluation uplift applied to council property assets, has not been applied to a category of existing use value assets and could become cumulatively material over five years. The council's previous year accounts received a clean bill of health from auditors.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - 2026-27 MTFS Budget Reductions Risk Tracker September 2026
findings.headline: Day Services re-commissioning (£50k) not delivering; business case still incomplete at midpoint of financial year
findings.detail: SSW7 proposes to save £50k by re-providing day opportunities for adults with learning disabilities in-house rather than through independent providers. The business case remains incomplete, and £0 has been achieved to date.
findings.matters: At the halfway point of the financial year, a proposal with zero delivery progress and an unfinished business case carries execution risk and may not deliver within the year.
findings.figures: £50k proposed, £0 achieved to date, business case status incomplete
findings.quote: Business Case is currently being completed for this proposal.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - 2026-27 MTFS Budget Reductions Risk Tracker September 2026
findings.headline: Climate Emergency Programme budget cut will impact Welsh Government net zero 2030 target
findings.detail: The £50k reduction (COM5) will force the Climate Emergency Programme to be remodelled. The council now expects to require additional external grant funding or partnership support to maintain its contribution to the Welsh Government's net zero 2030 target.
findings.matters: The council is now dependent on securing external funding to meet a Welsh Government statutory policy deadline; funding risk sits outside council control.
findings.figures: £50k reduction to Climate Emergency Response Programme; external funding now required
findings.quote: The Climate Emergency Programme will have to be remodelled. This will impact on the Welsh Government's net zero 2030 target and will now require additional grant funding from external sources or joint working with partners to achieve our ambitious targets.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - 2026-27 MTFS Budget Reductions Risk Tracker September 2026
findings.headline: Council implementing £140k of maintenance cuts despite assessing them as counter-productive to long-term asset operation
findings.detail: Two maintenance proposals (cyclical servicing review at £40k and corporate landlord maintenance reduction at £100k) are explicitly described in the council's own impact assessment as counter-productive for long-term asset operation. The council is proceeding with both to meet MTFS targets.
findings.matters: Trading long-term asset degradation for short-term savings creates risk of future capital pressures or remedial spending that may exceed current savings achieved.
findings.figures: COM2 £40k, COM6 £100k, total £140k of maintenance reductions identified as counter-productive
findings.quote: Reduction of cyclical maintenance activity counter productive for long term asset operation.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - 2026-27 MTFS Budget Reductions Risk Tracker September 2026
findings.headline: Social Services staff reduction paused due to demand pressure; savings now offset by underspends
findings.detail: A planned post deletion in business support services (SSW4, £129k saving) has been paused to maintain service resilience and manage increased demand. The council is offsetting the shortfall through staffing underspends rather than implementing the originally planned restructure.
findings.matters: Rising demand is constraining rather than enabling savings options; if demand continues or underspends exhaust, the council faces a hard choice between service resilience and MTFS delivery.
findings.figures: £129k proposed; post deletion paused due to demand; offset via staffing underspends
findings.quote: Increased demand has required the planned deletion of a further post to be paused to maintain service resilience and safely manage demand.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - 2026-27 MTFS Budget Reductions Risk Tracker September 2026
findings.headline: £620k of Adult Social Care savings conditional on permanent commissioning team funding not stated as secured
findings.detail: Two major ASC proposals—residential placement reviews (£370k) and direct payment reviews (£250k)—are listed as likely to be achieved but both are expressly conditional on securing permanent funding for the commissioning for complex needs team. SSW5 has achieved £0 despite being halfway through the financial year.
findings.matters: £620k of savings depend on internal funding commitments not mentioned as confirmed; lack of early progress on the £370k placement review suggests implementation risk.
findings.figures: SSW5 proposed £370k, achieved £0 to date; SSW6 proposed £250k, achieved £125k; both conditional on commissioning team funding
findings.quote: The delivery of these savings will only be achieved if there is permanent funding secured for the commissioning for complex needs team.

daily_post.headline: Bridgend's draft Minimum Revenue Provision was understated by £0.291 million relating to the Rhiw purchase, requiring correction during audit.
daily_post.lead: MRP controls are fundamental to a council's debt management; an understatement indicates potential pressure on capital financing resources or weaknesses in how capital transactions are accounted for.
